# The cast

7 characters, one per way in on the finder's spectrum plus the voice of the site and the agent that runs the interview. Three are shared with [the book's cast](https://storyboards.sgit.ai/gen-z-developers/cast.html), look unchanged, so the family of sites reads the same; four are this site's own. Every look is data in [`cast.json`](../cast.json), drawn by the kit; nothing is an image.

### Zara

the student: final year, no startup yet

*I do not have a startup. Is that allowed?*

### Inês

the designer with a notebook of twelve ideas

*I have twelve ideas. Which one?*

### Rui

the framework builder: one idea, three components deep, not shipped

*It is not ready yet.*

### Marta

the expert founder: twenty-five years as a pharmacist, a forty-page plan, starting a company

*Forty pages of plan. Tell me what to do.*

### Ana

the one who ships: a small tool three clinics already use, from a key she sends

*Three clinics use it. Now what?*

### The Guide

the voice of this site: says what the site says, in its words

*It is not ready yet is the problem, not the reason.*

### The Finder

the agent that runs the interview: Claude, ChatGPT or the page, following finder.json

*Where are you?*

## The model sheet

Every character in every mood and every pose the kit knows, so a storyboard's author can pick by eye.

The cast is a proposal for Dinis (`cast.json`, `what`). Characters use the pronouns their cast entry gives. A character's badge (explorer, villager, town planner) is a centre of gravity, not a box, as the book describes it.
